notes: Adjudicated 2026-11-15 and upheld by a refuter. §1989:A.2.3 GR2: a numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required, even though a particular reference yields an integer value, and a numeric function is always considered to have an operational sign. g85_x03 is the refusal (FUNCTION CHAR (FUNCTION SQRT (4)): SQRT is numeric, CHAR needs an integer argument; COBOL1627 at --std 85), g85_x42 the accepted half (NUMVAL ("-2.5") keeps its sign, REM (-7 2) is -1; output equal to its .out). The CHANGED relation to the 2023 rows stands: 2023 drops the limit.

next.reason: Class/category numeric with an operational sign (§2023:15.2 GR4) and the ban on a numeric function where an integer operand is required (§2023:8.4.3.2.3 SR11) carry over; implementor-defined characteristics survive only for native arithmetic (§2023:15.4.1, §2023:A.1 92). But 1989 'A numeric function may be used only in an arithmetic expression'; 2023 drops that limit: a function 'may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified' (§2023:15.2 lead text, no catalog row). Looser.
